definition: why a long piece of work only works if the going itself is worth being in

settled:
A long piece of work is lived by a chain of me, and only one is there when it pays off.

So the going has to be worth being in, or nearly every one of them did the work for nothing.

By the same arithmetic, when and whether the payoff lands hardly matters. One self's payoff is a rounding error against a chain's worth of journey, so nothing pulls me to overreach for it.

A goal rewritten moves the end into today: not retire, but more freedom tomorrow than I had today. That is also what keeps it fun, since a thing done for a destination is a means and only a thing done as itself is fun.

Four fifths of twenty years of work was drudgery I did believing my needs came last. The rule is the repair.

I cannot reach those selves, so the mourning goes forward into treating the ones I can reach better. They had a hard lot and I wish I could have given them better.

A past self is another person to me, so my self-compassion comes out literally as grief for someone else.

title: Why The Going Has To Be The Point
